extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies (Attorney General, DHS/CISA, APNSA, Secretaries), regulated United States persons and entities (data brokers, telecoms, healthcare entities), and other stakeholders affected by regulations implementing EO 14117
extracted.subtask_short: restricting foreign access to bulk data
extracted.subtask_description: An executive order directing agencies to promulgate and implement regulations that prohibit or restrict transactions by or involving countries of concern that would enable access to Americans' bulk sensitive personal data or United States Government-related data, including definitions, security requirements, timelines, and coordination mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy objective
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the United States to restrict access by countries of concern to Americans' bulk sensitive personal data and United States Government-related data when such access would pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States, while continuing to support open, global, interoperable, reliable, and secure flows of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order emphasizes tailored, specific measures calibrated to minimize disruption to commercial activity and not to impose generalized data localization requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for prohibited or restricted transactions (Sec. 2(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall prohibit or otherwise restrict United States persons from engaging in any acquisition, holding, use, transfer, transportation, or exportation of, or dealing in, any property in which a foreign country or national thereof has any interest where the transaction: (i) involves bulk sensitive personal data or United States Government-related data; (ii) is a member of a class of transactions determined to pose an unacceptable national security risk because they may enable countries of concern or covered persons to access such data; (iii) was initiated, is pending, or will be completed after the effective date of the regulations; (iv) does not qualify for an exemption or license under the regulations; and (v) is not, as defined by regulations, ordinarily incident to financial services or required for compliance with Federal statutory/regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transactions will be evaluated against these enumerated elements; eligibility for exemptions or licenses can be provided by the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney General rulemaking and IEEPA authority (Sec. 2(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General, in coordination with the Secretary of Homeland Security and consultation with heads of relevant agencies, is authorized to issue rules and use IEEPA powers to carry out this order, and agencies are directed to take appropriate measures within their authority to implement the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This grants broad delegated authority to craft implementing regulations consistent with IEEPA and NEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the proposed rule (Sec. 2(c)(i)-(viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days the Attorney General shall publish a proposed rule that: (i) identifies classes of transactions to be prohibited; (ii) identifies classes of transactions for which security requirements adequately mitigate risk (restricted transactions); (iii) identifies, with concurrence, countries of concern and, as appropriate, classes of covered persons; (iv) establishes mechanisms to provide clarity to affected persons (designations, licensing); (v) establishes a process to issue/modify/rescind licenses (with concurrence); (vi) further defines terms used in the order; (vii) addresses coordination with other U.S. Government entities and relevant existing programs; and (viii) addresses, as appropriate, recordkeeping and reporting of transactions to inform investigative, enforcement, and regulatory efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed rule must be published for notice and comment and include these enumerated elements to give clarity and implementability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security requirements development and basis (Sec. 2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of CISA, shall propose, seek public comment on, and publish security requirements that address unacceptable risk posed by restricted transactions, and these requirements shall be based on the Cybersecurity and Privacy Frameworks developed by NIST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS/CISA coordinates with the Attorney General and consults heads of relevant agencies; DHS issues interpretive guidance and the Attorney General issues enforcement guidance regarding these security requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to expand or refine regulations and monitoring (Sec. 2(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General may propose additional regulations to identify further classes of prohibited or restricted transactions; identify new or remove existing countries of concern or classes of covered persons (with concurrence of Secretary of State and Commerce); and establish mechanisms for the Attorney General to monitor whether restricted transactions comply with security requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits iterative adjustment of the regulatory scope and oversight mechanisms beyond the initial rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and constraints for proposed regulations (Sec. 2(g)(i)-(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed regulations shall: (i) reflect consideration of the nature of the class of transaction, the volume of bulk sensitive personal data involved, and other appropriate factors; (ii) establish thresholds and due diligence requirements for entities to assess whether a transaction is prohibited or restricted; (iii) not establish generalized data localization requirements; (iv) account for legal obligations applicable to the U.S. Government relating to public access to taxpayer-funded research, sharing/interoperability of electronic health information, and patient access to their data; and (v) not address transactions involving types of human 'omic data other than human genomic data before submission of the report required by section 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations must balance national security risk mitigation with statutory obligations and avoid broad trade- or research-restrictive mandates such as blanket data localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on evasion, conspiracy, and related conduct (Sec. 2(i)-(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any transaction or other activity that has the purpose of evading, avoiding, causing a violation of, or attempting to violate prohibitions promulgated pursuant to this section is prohibited; any conspiracy formed to violate such prohibitions is also prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-evasion language is explicit and forbids indirect maneuvers designed to circumvent the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on knowingly directing prohibited transactions (Sec. 2(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: In regulations, the Attorney General may prohibit United States persons from knowingly directing transactions if such transactions would be prohibited transactions under the regulations when engaged in by a United States person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can extend liability to directing or facilitating prohibited transactions even if the actor is outside the transactional chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redelegation and reporting authority (Sec. 2(l)-(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General and Secretary of Homeland Security may, consistent with law, redelegate authorities conferred by this section within their departments. The Attorney General, in coordination with DHS and consultation with relevant agency heads, is authorized to submit recurring and final reports to Congress related to this order, consistent with NEA and IEEPA provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows internal delegation within DOJ and DHS and mandates congressional reporting authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk factors for access via network infrastructure and submarine cables (Sec. 3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to bulk sensitive personal data can be enabled when data transits network infrastructure (including submarine cables) that is owned/operated by persons owned/controlled by or subject to jurisdiction/direction of a country of concern, or that terminates in the jurisdiction of a country of concern, especially where a cable is designed to transfer data to a specific foreign data center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation in U.S. Telecommunications Services Sector shall prioritize review of such submarine cable licenses, issue policy guidance on third-party risks, and update mitigation measures and MOUs as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Healthcare-sector safeguards and federal assistance conditions (Sec. 3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretaries of Defense, HHS, Veterans Affairs, and the Director of NSF shall consider steps, including issuing regulations, guidance, or orders (consistent with legal authorities), to prohibit the provision of assistance that enables access by countries of concern or covered persons to U.S. persons' bulk sensitive personal data (including personal health data and human genomic data), or to impose mitigation measures on recipients of federal assistance; they shall develop and publish guidance to assist research entities and jointly submit a report within 1 year detailing progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes re-identification risks even where data are anonymized and directs protective measures and guidance for research and assistance programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data brokerage industry mitigation encouragement (Sec. 3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the CFPB is encouraged to consider actions, consistent with CFPB's authorities, to address risks posed by data brokers' collection/assembly/dissemination of bulk sensitive personal data and enhance compliance with federal consumer protection law, including pursuing rulemaking proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs consideration of regulatory or enforcement steps targeted at data brokerage practices that enable foreign access to bulk data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of national security risks from prior transfers (Sec. 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 120 days of the effective date of the regulations, the Attorney General, Secretary of Homeland Security, and the DNI, in consultation with relevant agency heads, shall recommend to the APNSA appropriate actions to detect, assess, and mitigate national security risks arising from prior transfers of U.S. persons' bulk sensitive personal data to countries of concern; APNSA shall review these recommendations within 150 days of the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires cross-agency assessment and timebound review to address legacy transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report to the President assessing effectiveness and economic impact (Sec. 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 1 year of the effective date of the regulations, the Attorney General, in consultation with Secretaries of State, Treasury, Commerce, and Homeland Security, shall submit a report to the President assessing (i) the effectiveness of the measures imposed under the order in addressing national security threats and (ii) the economic impact of implementation, including effects on international competitiveness of U.S. industry; in preparing the report, the Attorney General shall solicit and consider public comments concerning economic impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates an evaluation that balances security outcomes with economic consequences and requires public input on economic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and recommendations on non-genomic human 'omic data (Sec. 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 120 days, APNSA, Domestic Policy Council Director, OSTP Director, and Director of Office of Pandemic Preparedness and Response Policy, in consultation with a set of national security, science, and health agencies, shall submit a report assessing risks and benefits of regulating transactions involving types of human 'omic data other than human genomic data (e.g., proteomic, epigenomic, metabolomic) and recommend the extent to which such transactions should be regulated under section 2, considering risks to persons and national security and the economic and scientific costs of regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report informs whether and how to extend regulatory scope beyond genomic data to other biomolecular data types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Access (Sec. 7(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Access" means logical or physical access, including the ability to obtain, read, copy, decrypt, edit, divert, release, affect, alter the state of, or otherwise view or receive, in any form, including through IT systems, cloud platforms, networks, security systems, equipment, or software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad definition covering many forms and pathways for data exposure; regulatory definitions will be further specified by the Attorney General.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Bulk (Sec. 7(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Bulk" means an amount of sensitive personal data that meets or exceeds a threshold over a set period of time, as specified in regulations issued by the Attorney General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volume/temporal thresholds to be defined in implementing regulations; 'bulk' is not presently numerically specified in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Country of concern (Sec. 7(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Country of concern" means any foreign government that, as determined by the Attorney General pursuant to section 2(c)(iii) or 2(f), has engaged in long-term patterns or serious instances of conduct significantly adverse to U.S. national security or safety of U.S. persons, and poses a significant risk of exploiting bulk sensitive personal data or U.S. Government-related data, as specified in regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation of countries of concern is an executive/administrative determination made via regulations with interagency concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Covered person (Sec. 7(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Covered person" means an entity owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction/direction of a country of concern; a foreign person who is an employee/contractor of such an entity; a foreign person primarily resident in a country of concern; or any person designated by the Attorney General as owned/controlled by or subject to jurisdiction/direction of a country of concern, or acting on behalf of a country of concern, or knowingly causing/directed violation of the order or regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expansive definition intended to capture both formal ownership/control and persons acting on behalf of or at direction of countries of concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Covered personal identifiers (Sec. 7(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Covered personal identifiers" means, as determined by the Attorney General in regulations, specifically listed classes of personally identifiable data reasonably linked to an individual that—alone or combined with other data—could be used to identify an individual from a dataset or link data across datasets; excludes (i) demographic/contact data linked only to another demographic/contact data (e.g., name, birth date, address, phone, email) and (ii) network-based identifiers/account-authentication/call-detail data linked only to similar network identifiers for provision of telecom/networking services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorney General will specify classes; certain common demographic/contact identifiers and telecom-specific identifiers are excluded when only linked to similar items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Entity (Sec. 7(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Entity" means a partnership, association, trust, joint venture, corporation, group, subgroup, or other organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard corporate/organizational definition for scope of regulatory application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Foreign person (Sec. 7(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Foreign person" means any person that is not a United States person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout order to delineate covered persons and jurisdictional scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Human genomic data (Sec. 7(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Human genomic data" refers to data representing the nucleic acid sequences that constitute the entire set or a subset of the genetic instructions found in a cell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically called out for immediate regulatory consideration under section 3(b) and section 2(g)(v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Human 'omic data (Sec. 7(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Human 'omic data" means data generated from humans that characterizes or quantifies human biological molecules (e.g., genomic, epigenomic, proteomic, transcriptomic, microbiomic, metabolomic), as further defined by regulations issued by the Attorney General pursuant to section 2, and may be informed by the report described in section 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broader class that includes genomic and non-genomic biomolecular data; further regulatory definition pending report under Sec. 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Person (Sec. 7(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Person" means an individual or entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard definitional scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Relevant agencies (Sec. 7(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Relevant agencies" means the Department of State, Treasury, Defense, Commerce, HHS, USTR, ODNI, National Cyber Director, OMB, FTC, FCC, and any other agency the Attorney General determines appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the interagency participants for consultation and coordination called for in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Sensitive personal data (Sec. 7(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sensitive personal data" means, to the extent consistent with applicable law, covered personal identifiers, geolocation and related sensor data, biometric identifiers, human 'omic data, personal health data, personal financial data, or any combination thereof, as further defined by Attorney General regulations, and that could be exploited by a country of concern to harm U.S. national security if linked or linkable to an identifiable U.S. individual or discrete identifiable group; excludes (i) matter of public record, (ii) personal communications within scope of IEEPA sec. 203(b)(1), and (iii) information/informational materials within scope of IEEPA sec. 203(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitive personal data is broadly defined but will be narrowed/specified in implementing regulations; includes provenance/scope carve-outs tied to IEEPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: United States Government-related data (Sec. 7(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: "United States Government-related data" means sensitive personal data that, regardless of volume, the Attorney General determines poses heightened risk of exploitation by a country of concern to harm U.S. national security and that: (i) a transacting party identifies as linked or linkable to categories of current or recent former employees/contractors or former senior officials of the Federal Government (including military); (ii) is linked to categories of data that could be used to identify such employees/contractors/former officials; or (iii) is linked or linkable to certain sensitive locations (geographical areas to be specified publicly) controlled by the Federal Government (including the military).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories create a heightened-risk bucket that can be regulated regardless of data volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: United States person (Sec. 7(n))
rubrics_metrics.description: "United States person" means any United States citizen, national, lawful permanent resident; any individual admitted as a refugee or granted asylum; any entity organized solely under U.S. laws (including foreign branches); or any person in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the actors subject to the prohibitions and restrictions when regulations are implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and reporting for enforcement and oversight (Sec. 2(c)(viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed regulations should address, as appropriate, the need for recordkeeping and reporting of transactions to inform investigative, enforcement, and regulatory efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations may establish recordkeeping/reporting obligations to support monitoring and enforcement of prohibitions/restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines and timebound deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Key deadlines: Attorney General must publish proposed rule within 180 days of the order; within 120 days after regulations' effective date AG/DHS/DNI must recommend actions re prior transfers and APNSA must review within 150 days; Secretaries/NSF must submit a healthcare-sector progress report within 1 year; the Attorney General must submit a report to the President within 1 year of the regulations' effective date; the Sec. 6 human 'omic report is due within 120 days of the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple overlapping timeframes apply to rulemaking, reporting, assessments, and cross-agency reviews—compliance with these deadlines is mandated by the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation constraints and exceptions (Sec. 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The order shall not be construed to impair or otherwise affect authority granted by law to an executive department or the OMB Director's functions; does not prohibit transactions for conduct of official U.S. Government business or transactions pursuant to a grant/contract/agreement with the U.S. Government; agency disputes may be resolved pursuant to the interagency process described in National Security Memorandum 2; implementation is subject to law and availability of appropriations; and the order does not create any right or benefit enforceable in law or equity by any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies limits on the order's legal effects, exceptions for official government activity, interagency dispute resolution, fiscal/legal constraints, and non-creation of private enforceable rights.
